title: Multiprotocol hosted inference surface: single-surface API for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank + launch readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Deliver a single, clearly documented hosted inference surface that supports chat, single-turn completions, embeddings, and rerank workflows while preserving semantics customers expect from dedicated endpoints. This ticket defines product requirements, acceptance criteria, launch checklist, and rollout strategy for GA of the multiprotocol surface. The goal is to reduce surface area and simplify onboarding while providing explicit compatibility guarantees for existing hosted customers.
goals: Provide a single API surface ("generate") that supports explicit modes: chat, completion, embedding, rerank
Preserve backwards-compatible contracts for existing hosted endpoints for at least one release cycle
Ship SDK patches and docs that allow customers to migrate with minimal code changes (migration guide + automated code snippets)

Ensure production SLOs: median token latency < 80ms for short-context completions; p95 < 300ms under normal load for chat; embeddings throughput and 99th percentile latency targets defined per model tier
Complete security review, rate-limit baseline, and cost-exposure guardrails prior to GA
non_goals: Building a single runtime binary that merges all model formats (this is an API surface change only)
Major changes to Dedicated/Private product contracts (aside from parity documentation and migration guides)
Significant changes to model catalog or introducing new model architecture—will rely on existing model onboarding work
scope_included: API contract specification for 'generate' endpoint with explicit mode parameter and mode-specific fields
SDK updates (JavaScript, Python, Go) that expose new mode flags and migration helpers
Launch docs: PRD, migration guide, examples for chat->mode="chat" and existing completions users
End-to-end tests and load tests for each mode with representative payloads
Console UI updates: per-mode cost/lantency breakdowns and per-route dashboards
Rollout plan: staged canary across 5%->25%->100% with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
scope_excluded: Rewriting existing customer SDKs to use the new endpoint automatically (we provide code snippets but not auto-migrations)
Changes to Dedicated capacity billing or contract language (handled by enterprise ops)
On-prem private control-plane distribution changes in this release
api_contract_summary: Top-level fields: model, mode, input (string or structured chat array), stream (boolean), max_tokens, temperature, top_p, metadata (object) - metadata must be RFC-compliant JSON string in header
Response shape: standardized envelope { request_id, model, mode, duration_ms, usage: { input_tokens, output_tokens }, result } where result is mode-specific
Chat mode: result.chat: array of message objects with role, content, optional function call structure
Completion mode: result.text (string) with token-level logprobs if requested
Embedding mode: result.embedding: array of floats (stringified in JSON to prevent precision loss in some SDKs), plus vector_id optional
Rerank mode: client sends list of candidates and query, response returns ranked candidate IDs with scores and normalized confidence
Streaming: chat and completion support chunked streaming; embedding and rerank do not stream
Backwards compatibility: legacy endpoints continue active for one release cycle and return deprecation headers pointing to new path and migration doc
acceptance_criteria: API contract validated with conformance tests: postman collection and integration tests pass for all modes
SDK patches released and passing CI: JS/TS >= 1.14.0, Python >= 0.18.0, Go >= 0.9.3
Latency SLOs met in staging under representative load: median token latency < 80ms for short completions; chat p95 < 300ms
Streaming semantics preserved: clients receive message chunks in order with no duplication on retries
Usage and billing metrics correctly emitted: per-mode usage breakdowns appear in Console and billing export
Feature flag gating behaves: controlled rollout toggles enable percent-based traffic shifts and automated rollback on SLO threshold breaches
Security sign-off completed and pen-test findings remediated or documented with mitigations
Migration guide reviewed by Developer Docs and Developer Relations and includes at least two real code examples per SDK
E2E smoke tests for rerank include > 95% precision on canonical dataset used for CI
Rate limiting policy applied and tested: soft quota enforcement + clear 429 semantics + guidance for client retry backoff
launch_checklist: Docs: Finalized API reference page, migration guide, release notes, FAQ
SDK Releases: JS, Python, Go published to npm/pypi/gomod with migration helpers
Samples: Updated quickstarts and three sample apps (chat app, search+rerank demo, semantic search using embeddings)
Console: per-mode dashboard tiles, cost breakdown by route, rollout controls visible
Observability: dashboards for latency, errors, throughput per-mode; synthetic monitors for each mode; alert thresholds set
Load testing: run 72-hour soak at expected 2x production QPS per-mode; document findings
Security: completed review, secrets handling verified, KMS integration smoke tested
Billing: cost center estimates, per-mode cost multipliers documented, billing export validated
Support: runbook for migration issues, triage playbook for latency regressions, slack channel #prod-api-launch created
Enterprise: notify Dedicated/Private accounts, publish migration timeline and compatibility guarantees
Legal/Compliance: updated ToS if needed and privacy checklist completed
Feature gating: create feature flag and rollout schedule; prepare canary rollback plan
Release communication: blog post draft, changelog, email templates for high-usage customers
rollout_plan: Three-stage rollout: 1) Internal + infra canaries (1 day) 2) External canary (5% traffic, 3 days) with aggressive telemetry and manual gate 3) Progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers for p95 latency, error rate, or cost-risk anomalies. Post-100%: two-week monitoring window with weekly check-ins.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Streaming regressions cause client-visible breaks - Mitigation: maintain exact streaming contract and run compatibility tests against known client libraries
Risk: Customers rely on legacy endpoint shape - Mitigation: dual-run for one release cycle with deprecation headers and migration help
Risk: Rerank costs explode for large candidate sets - Mitigation: enforce candidate-size defaults, document cost guidance, provide server-side sampling helper
Risk: Embedding precision/formatting mismatch across SDKs - Mitigation: standardized serialization approach (base64 or JSON string) and SDK serializers
Risk: Unexpected latency regressions at scale - Mitigation: staged rollout, autoscaling safety caps, and canary-based rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for contract validation across modes
Integration tests exercising streaming paths and reconnection/retry behavior
Performance tests: p95/p99 token latency benchmarks across representative models and sequence lengths
Chaos tests: simulate KV cache misses, spike QPS, and regional failover scenarios
Rerank correctness tests against curated datasets and A/B comparisons to existing endpoint
notes: This PRD prioritizes predictability for end users who maintain legacy integrations while enabling a simpler, single-surface developer experience for new customers. Teams should coordinate messaging to high-usage accounts before canary expansion. Any substantive change to the API contract post-approval must re-open the security review checkbox and re-run conformance tests.
